response: Increasing blood pH has been found not to have a positive effect on albumin and muscle protein synthesis, as well as nutritional and endocrine parameters, in dialysis patients. Specifically, higher blood pH levels were associated with increased BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen) levels and low salivary flow rates, which can be indicators of halitosis (bad breath). Studies suggest that peritoneal dialysis may play a role in decreasing the level of halitosis in end-stage renal disease patients.
